info.name: PIL Announcements API
info.description:
Functional and conformance tests for the announcements microservice.

**Run order matters.** `Setup` fetches an OAuth 2.0 access token and `Create` seeds the announcements that `List` pages through, so run the whole collection rather than individual requests:

```
newman run postman/announcements.postman_collection.json \
  -e postman/announcements.postman_environment.json
```

Fill the environment file from a deployed stack with `./scripts/show_credentials.sh --json`.

Every request also inherits the collection-level tests, which assert the invariants the PIL RESTful API Guidelines place on *every* response: JSON content type, a JSON API document at the root, `data` and `errors` never coexisting, error objects carrying a code from the standard list, and no internal failure detail in the body.

item.name: 4. Guideline conformance
item.description: Obligations the PIL RESTful API Guidelines place on every API.

item.name: Missing Api-Version is 400
item.description: The guidelines require a request without a version to be rejected.

item.name: Unsupported Api-Version is 400
item.description: An unknown major version is rejected rather than served on a guess.

item.name: Missing Api-Key is 403
item.description: Client identification is mandatory on every method.

item.name: Invalid Api-Key is 403
item.description: An unrecognised key is refused with the same status but a distinct code.

item.name: An Accept header we cannot satisfy is 406
item.description: The API only produces JSON.

item.name: An unsupported method is 405
item.description: DELETE is not part of the contract, so the resource says so explicitly instead of leaking an authentication error.

exec: pm.test('status is 405 Method Not Allowed', () => pm.response.to.have.status(405));
